newsitem.title: UK: Copper has good support on LME, nickel watches Inco.
newsitem.headline: Copper has good support on LME, nickel watches Inco.

text.p: Copper prices continued to draw good support from low world stocks and nickel traders closely watched developments at Inco labour talks ahead of a contract expiry midnight Saturday.
But most other metals were on the defensive with technicals pointing to the possibility of further losses.
Three months delivery copper reached a one year high of $2,545 a tonne in the rings before light profittaking saw it end the kerb at $2,540, up $12 from Thursday.
Traders said the very low level of world copper stocks, at less than four weeks consumption, made the market very vulnerable to supply hitches and discouraged players from shorting the market.
But technical traders reckoned prices need to break above $2,540/$2,550 resistance to maintain its upward momentum or else its overbought indicators could start to weigh heavily on the market.
Latest news from Inco said the union was not optimistic despite pay talks with managament continuing.
"Let me tell you, unless there is something substantial on the table today, operations are down, and I can't put it any plainer than that,' union vice-president Gary Patterson said.
The labout contract expires at midnight Saturday and the union has a strike mandate from its members.
But three months nickel ended the morning trading at $7,250 down $30 a tonne after a 1,000 tonnes-plus LME stocks rise.

Zinc stocks rose 1,550 tonnes with more metal arriving in Singapore as high prices attracted Chinese zinc and this, coupled with overbought technical signals, could prompt a correction of around $50 according to some traders.
Three months zinc ended the morning at $1,347, down $10 from Thursday.
Aluminium was another metal which some technical traders reckoned needed a sell-off to clear the air.
Persistent resistance around the $1,640/$1,650 level had blunted the market's overall uptrend and led to the possibility of three months breaking below $1,610, triggering further selling.
Three months aluminium last traded at $1,619, down $8.
Tin held just above Thursday's 26 month lows with a small stocks fall possibly relieving the downward pressure for the time being, traders said.
Brokers Macquarie said in a market report that Chinese tin exports have risen since last year and have pushed the market back into surplus.
Last tin business was at $5,580, down $20.
Lead drifted lower to end at $634, down $6, and alloy was last quoted at $1,485/$1,490, little changed.
